label: lem:antiderivatives_diff_constant
title: Two antiderivatives differ by a constant
statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $F, G$ both be antiderivatives of $f$ on $\mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; b$ (i.e.\ $\texttt{IsAntiderivativeOn}\; F\; f\; a\; b$ and $\texttt{IsAntiderivativeOn}\; G\; f\; a\; b$), with both $F$ and $G$ continuous on $\mathrm{Icc}\; a\; b$. Then $F - G$ is constant on $\mathrm{Icc}\; a\; b$, i.e., for all $x \in \mathrm{Icc}\; a\; b$, $(F - G)(x) = (F - G)(a)$.
proof: Since $F$ and $G$ are both antiderivatives of $f$ on $\mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; b$, for every $x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; b$ we have $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; F\; (f\;x)\; x$ and $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; G\; (f\;x)\; x$. By the linearity of derivatives (\texttt{HasDerivAt.sub}), $F - G$ has derivative $f(x) - f(x) = 0$ at every $x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; b$. Moreover, $F - G$ is continuous on $\mathrm{Icc}\; a\; b$ since both $F$ and $G$ are. By Lemma~\ref{lem:zero_deriv_constant}, $(F-G)(x) = (F-G)(a)$ for all $x \in \mathrm{Icc}\; a\; b$.
